topic: Role-based work queues / 'my work' inboxes in enterprise workflow software: surfacing 'what needs me now', next-step guidance, empty states, and separating action queues from read-only record browsing (applied to ERIS)

findings.principle: A personal work queue should be grouped by a curated 'focus order' rather than by creation date or ID. Linear's My Issues > Assigned tab groups work as 'urgent work, SLA-bound work, blockers, cycle work, other active work, triage, backlog, and completed work', ordered by priority within each group with started (in-progress) issues first. The view also separates Assigned / Created / Subscribed / Activity into tabs.
findings.applicability: ERIS 'My Work' should be the default landing page for every role and group rows as: Overdue or emergency-flagged incidents; items with an assessment/review due date; items blocked or waiting on someone else; in-progress GISA drafts (engineers) or in-progress reviews (reviewers); newly assigned/unrouted items; completed (collapsed). Within each group, sort by severity then due date, with anything the user has already started at the top so an engineer returning from the field lands on the draft they were editing.

findings.principle: Keep the shared team inbox separate from the personal queue. Linear's Triage is 'a special inbox for your team' where items from integrations or outside members land; the reviewer has exactly four actions — Accept (move into the workflow), Decline (cancel with reason), Mark as duplicate (merge into an existing issue), and Snooze (hide until a chosen time or until new activity). Its purpose is 'to review, update, and prioritize issues before they are added to your team's workflow'.
findings.applicability: Maintenance coordinators need a dedicated 'Field reports' triage inbox distinct from 'My Work'. Each new field report gets the same four verbs: Accept (create/attach to a geotechnical incident and send for routing), Decline (not a geotech matter, with reason kept on record), Merge (same slope/site reported twice after a storm), Snooze (waiting for photos or a callback, auto-returns when the reporter adds information). This keeps unvetted reports out of chiefs' routing queues.

findings.principle: Make triage ownership explicit and rotatable. Linear lets teams 'define who handles incoming issues' via triage responsibility, supports rotating first responders through on-call integrations, and shows who is currently assigned to monitor triage at the moment someone files an issue.
findings.applicability: ERIS staff rotate. Show 'Triage on duty: <name>' in the district/branch header and on the field-report submission confirmation, let office/branch chiefs set a rotation or backup, and route new-report notifications to the on-duty person rather than a static role list so reports do not stall when the usual coordinator is out.

findings.principle: Default queues should be organized by ownership state. Jira Service Management ships every service project with 'All open', 'Assigned to me', 'Unassigned', and 'Resolved' queues; agents sort, assign, and bulk-update work items directly from a queue, and queues can be grouped for prioritization.
findings.applicability: For GeoTech office/branch chiefs, 'Unassigned' (needs routing) must be a first-class queue distinct from 'Assigned to me' and 'Assigned to my branch'. Support bulk 'Assign to engineer' and 'Route to branch' from that queue, because a single storm can produce dozens of incidents that are routed in one sitting.

findings.principle: Prefer multiple simple queues over one complex one, and show only recent work by default. Atlassian's guidance for queues at scale: 'Often it is better to have multiple simple queues than one complex one', avoid queues that analyse across many custom fields, and restrict queues to recent items (e.g. updated within 14 days).
findings.applicability: Replace a single 'All incidents' mega-table with named, stage-specific queues per role — 'Needs routing', 'Awaiting my review', 'Returned for revision', 'Draft GISA forms', 'Approvals due' — each with a small fixed column set. The read-only browse table defaults to items updated in the last 90 days with an explicit 'Show all history' toggle.

findings.principle: Empty states in complex applications must (1) communicate system status, (2) provide learning cues about what the area is for, and (3) offer direct pathways to key tasks. NN/g specifically warns against briefly showing 'No records' before content loads, which 'leads to user frustration or abandoned tasks' and erodes trust.
findings.applicability: Every ERIS queue needs three distinct states: loading (skeleton rows, never the empty message), truly empty ('No incidents need routing right now. New field reports appear here automatically after the coordinator accepts them.' + link 'Browse all incidents'), and filtered-empty ('No results for District 4 + Awaiting review' + 'Clear filters'). Do not render the empty message until the query has resolved.

findings.principle: Empty-state copy should state the reason for the emptiness and where the user can go next; when there is genuinely nothing to do, 'celebrate finishing a task'. Keep the message to one or two sentences, use a scannable sentence-case title, and avoid jargon.
findings.applicability: An empty 'My Work' for a reviewer should read 'You're all caught up' with a one-line explanation ('Assessments sent to you for approval will appear here') and a tertiary link to the browse view. Never surface internal status codes or workflow enum names in these messages — rotating staff will not know them.

findings.principle: Carbon distinguishes three empty-state families — no-data/first-use, user-action (no search results, process completed), and error/permission (data exists but cannot be shown) — with an anatomy of image, title, body, primary action, secondary action. 'Keep words to a minimum so they are fast to read and act upon'; when several empty states appear on one page use tertiary buttons so the page is not cluttered with primary actions; never create dead ends.
findings.applicability: Role dashboards in ERIS that show several queue panels side by side (e.g. chief: Needs routing / My branch / Overdue) should use tertiary-weight actions inside each empty panel. A permission-based empty state (an engineer opening a reviewers-only queue) should say why it is empty and whom to contact, not show a blank table.

findings.principle: For long services users cannot finish in one sitting, use a task list: each section is a whole-row link with a status tag (e.g. Completed, Incomplete, Cannot start yet), short hint text, and completed items visually de-emphasized ('Completed' shown as plain text with no coloured background to emphasise remaining work). GOV.UK advises: 'If you're finding it difficult to come up with a clear and concise task name, it might be because the task itself is too complex', and not to use the pattern when a strict order is required.
findings.applicability: The GISA technical form should open as a section task list (Site and location, Photos, Geology and observations, Map and cross-section, Analysis, Recommendations, Sign-off) with status tags and 'You have completed X of Y sections'. Field-capturable sections (photos, location, map) can be done on iPad on site; office sections at the desk; Sign-off shows 'Cannot start yet' until required sections are complete. Use a separate summary view for the reviewer rather than reusing the task list.

findings.principle: Wizards suit 'novice users or infrequent processes'. NN/g's guidelines: show a step indicator with clearly labeled steps and the current step; make each step self-sufficient; use step-specific button labels; and allow save-and-resume because 'interruptions happen, and users should be able to save their work and later continue the process from where they left'.
findings.applicability: ERIS users are rotating, infrequent public-sector staff, so guided steps beat a monolithic form. Auto-save GISA drafts on every field change; the 'My Work' row for a draft should deep-link to the last incomplete section with a stage-specific label ('Continue: Photos (3 of 7)') rather than a generic 'Open'.

findings.principle: Workflow disruption comes from 'irritating detours and burdensome extra steps' — interstitials, forced confirmations, and systems that forget the user's context after an interruption and make them start over. Nielsen calls workflow 'one of the most important elements of application design'.
findings.applicability: After a coordinator accepts a report or a chief routes an incident, return them to the same scroll position in the queue with the next item ready — do not reset to the top or bounce to a record page. Avoid confirmation modals for routine, reversible queue actions (use undo instead); preserve unsaved form state across iPad connectivity drops and session timeouts.

findings.principle: Visibility of system status: 'a lack of information often equates to a lack of control'. Systems should keep users informed through timely feedback, display unavailable items rather than silently removing them, and use indicators for backstage events that affect the user.
findings.applicability: Every queue row should carry a workflow-stage badge and an age ('Awaiting reviewer for 3 days'). When an item leaves a user's queue because someone else acted (a chief routes it, a reviewer returns it), keep it visible briefly as 'Routed to Branch B' or in an Activity/Following tab instead of having it vanish, so coordinators can confirm their report made it downstream.

findings.principle: Match the communication channel to the message: indicators (badges, counts) are passive and contextual; validations demand immediate correction; notifications report system events and should be intrusive only when action is required. A validation or action-required message 'shouldn't be a dismissible toast' that users can miss, and routine events should not interrupt with modals.
findings.applicability: Show passive count badges on 'My Work' and 'Needs routing' in the ERIS navigation. Events that require action — 'GISA returned for revision', 'assessment awaiting your approval' — must persist as inbox rows, not just toasts. Reserve modal interruption for genuine emergencies such as an incident escalated to a road-closure/imminent-failure level.

findings.principle: Applied filters should be visible in an overview with clear-all and individual removal (20% of sites fail this in Baymard's benchmark); users should be able to select multiple values within one filter category; sidebar filters that expose options and counts up front are discovered more reliably than collapsed horizontal toolbars.
findings.applicability: The read-only ERIS record browser (Incidents, Assessments, Users) should show applied-filter chips (District, Status, Date range, Assigned to, Route/PM) with 'Clear all', allow multi-select statuses, show the result count, and on iPad use a filter drawer that reports how many records match before it is closed.

findings.principle: Esri's Calcite Table guidance: enable row selection only 'when there are associated user interactions' and expose contextual bulk actions through the selection-actions slot; 'Avoid using selectionMode when there are no associated user interactions'. Use Table for row/column data and List for simpler collections; paginate large datasets with a reasonable page size but avoid pagination for small sets.
findings.applicability: ERIS already sits on the Esri stack. Action queues (Needs routing, Approvals) are selectable tables with bulk Assign/Route/Approve in the selection-actions area; the read-only browse table should have no checkboxes unless a bulk export exists. On phones, render queues as a Calcite-style List/card stack rather than a wide table.

patterns.pattern: Role-scoped 'My Work' inbox with focus-order grouping and one primary next-step action per row
patterns.whenToUse: Whenever a signed-in user can be assigned work. Modeled on Linear My Issues (urgent > SLA > blocked > active > triage > backlog > done, started items first) and Asana My Tasks (Recently assigned / Today / Upcoming / Later sections auto-sorted by rules so users 'can prioritize what's next').
patterns.erisApplication: Make 'My Work' the post-login landing page for every role. Groups: Overdue and emergency-flagged; Due this week; In progress (my drafts/reviews); Waiting on others; New to me; Done (collapsed). Each row shows incident ID, site/route, stage badge, age, and exactly one stage-specific verb button: coordinator 'Accept', chief 'Route', engineer 'Continue (Section 4 of 7)', reviewer 'Review', admin 'Activate user'. Tabs: Assigned / Created / Following / Activity, kept to at most five, with two visual cues on the active tab per NN/g.

patterns.pattern: Shared Triage inbox with Accept / Decline / Merge / Snooze and a visible on-duty owner
patterns.whenToUse: When items arrive from outside the workflow team (public or field submissions, integrations) and must be vetted before entering routing. Modeled on Linear Triage.
patterns.erisApplication: Maintenance coordinators' 'Field reports' inbox. Accept creates or attaches to an incident and sends it to the chief's routing queue; Decline requires a reason and keeps the record searchable; Merge links duplicate reports of the same slope; Snooze hides until a date or until the reporter adds photos. Header shows 'Triage on duty: <name>' set by the chief with a backup.

patterns.pattern: Ownership-state queues (Unassigned / Assigned to me / Assigned to my group / Resolved) with bulk actions
patterns.whenToUse: For routing and supervisory roles who dispatch work to others. Modeled on Jira Service Management default queues and ServiceNow workspace list options (Open Unassigned, Assigned to me, Assigned to my group).
patterns.erisApplication: GeoTech office/branch chiefs land on 'Unassigned' by default, with 'Assigned to my branch' and 'Assigned to me' as sibling queues. Rows are selectable so a chief can pick ten post-storm incidents and bulk 'Assign to engineer' or 'Route to branch' from the selection-actions bar.

patterns.pattern: Section task list inside the long form, with status tags and 'X of Y sections complete'
patterns.whenToUse: Forms that cannot be completed in one sitting and whose sections can be done in any order. Modeled on the GOV.UK task list component (whole-row links, sentence-case status tags, de-emphasized 'Completed', short hint text).
patterns.erisApplication: GISA form landing page lists sections with statuses (Not yet started / In progress / Completed / Cannot start yet). Photo, location, and map sections are flagged as field-capturable for iPad use; Sign-off is 'Cannot start yet' until required sections are complete. The reviewer gets a separate read-only summary, not the task list.

patterns.whenToUse: Any multi-step task performed by infrequent users or interrupted in the field. Modeled on NN/g wizard guidance (save and resume, visible step indicator) and NN/g disruptive-workflow guidance (remember context).
patterns.erisApplication: Autosave GISA drafts on every change; the 'My Work' row deep-links to the last incomplete section with the section name and progress in the button label. After completing a queue action, return the user to the same queue position with the next item highlighted instead of navigating away.

patterns.pattern: Three-tier empty states with loading skeletons
patterns.whenToUse: Every queue, table, and dashboard panel. Combines NN/g (status + learning cue + pathway, never flash 'No records' while loading), Atlassian (reason + where next, celebrate when done, 1-2 sentences), and Carbon (no-data vs user-action vs error/permission; tertiary buttons when several panels are empty).
patterns.erisApplication: Loading: skeleton rows. Nothing to do: 'You're all caught up' + one line on what will appear here + tertiary 'Browse all assessments'. Filtered-empty: 'No results for these filters' + 'Clear filters'. Permission/error: 'You don't have access to Reviewer approvals — contact your branch chief' or 'Couldn't load the queue — Retry'. Never use internal status codes.

patterns.pattern: Separate 'Work' (action queues) from 'Records' (read-only browse) in navigation
patterns.whenToUse: When users both act on items and look things up. Queues are stage-specific, selectable, and carry next-step CTAs; browse views are filterable, paginated, and non-selectable. Grounded in Calcite Table selection guidance, Baymard applied-filter guidance, and NN/g's rule not to mix in-page tabs with navigation tabs.
patterns.erisApplication: Primary navigation: Work (My Work, Field reports, Needs routing, Approvals) and Records (Incidents, Assessments, Users). Records tables have applied-filter chips with 'Clear all', multi-select status, result counts, and no checkboxes unless bulk export exists. Queue tabs (Assigned / Following / Activity) stay inside the queue page; 'Browse all' is a navigation link, never a tab in the same control.

patterns.pattern: Stage badge + age + handoff trace on every row
patterns.whenToUse: Multi-role workflows where an item passes between people and users need to confirm it moved downstream. Grounded in NN/g visibility of system status (do not remove items silently; use indicators for backstage events).
patterns.erisApplication: Each row shows the workflow stage badge and 'in this stage for N days'. When an item leaves the user's queue because someone else acted, show it as 'Routed to Branch B on Sep 3' in a Following/Activity tab for a period. Reviewers see 'Waiting on you since ...' so overdue approvals are obvious.

patterns.pattern: Channel-matched notifications: badge counts, persistent inbox rows, modals only for emergencies
patterns.whenToUse: Whenever the system needs to tell a user something happened. Grounded in NN/g indicators/validations/notifications.
patterns.erisApplication: Nav badges for My Work and Needs routing counts; persistent inbox rows (with the next-step verb) for 'Returned for revision' and 'Awaiting your approval'; toasts only for confirmations with undo; a blocking modal only when an incident is escalated to emergency severity.

patterns.pattern: Recent-by-default with explicit 'show all', and small fixed column sets per queue
patterns.whenToUse: When queue and browse tables grow beyond a screenful. Grounded in Jira queues-at-scale guidance (simple queues, recent items only) and Calcite pagination guidance.
patterns.erisApplication: Queues show only open work. Records browse defaults to 'updated in last 90 days' in the user's district with a visible toggle to show all history. Each queue has at most six columns chosen for its decision (e.g. Needs routing: ID, site/route, severity, reported, reporter, suggested branch).

antiPatterns: One giant 'All incidents' table for every role with a dozen filters and no role-specific default queue (contradicts Jira's 'multiple simple queues' guidance and Linear's focus-order model).
Sorting 'my work' by creation date or record ID instead of urgency, due date, and in-progress state.
Flashing 'No records found' before the query resolves (NN/g: creates distrust and abandoned tasks).
Empty states that are dead ends: no explanation of why the list is empty and no link to the next place to go; or empty-state copy that uses internal workflow status codes and jargon.
Silently removing an item from a coordinator's or engineer's view after a handoff, with no trace that it was routed, returned, or approved.
Delivering action-required events ('returned for revision', 'approval needed') only as dismissible toasts rather than persistent inbox rows.
Modal confirmations and interstitials on routine, reversible queue actions (accept, route, assign) that break the triage rhythm.
Mixing 'Browse all' and 'My Work' as tabs in one tab control (NN/g: mixing navigation tabs with in-page tabs disorients users); tab labels in ALL CAPS.
Checkboxes and selection mode on read-only browse tables that offer no bulk action (Calcite: avoid selectionMode without associated interactions).
Filter UIs with no applied-filter overview or 'Clear all', or single-value-only status filters (Baymard).
Forcing strict sequential completion of the whole GISA form when field and office sections are done in different sittings and on different devices; no autosave or resume.
Showing 'Completed' sections with the same visual weight as remaining work, hiding what still needs doing (GOV.UK de-emphasizes Completed).
No visible triage owner or rotation, so new field reports stall when the usual coordinator is out.
Overloaded queue columns and complex multi-field queue definitions that are slow and hard to scan (Jira queues-at-scale guidance).
